database_overlap.why: CRAFT does not ship its training table, so which archives it drew on cannot be verified from the artefact. The paper text is the only source for that claim, and a claim is not a dataset.

molecule_overlap.unmeasurable: the remaining ~1380 training molecules are not shipped, so the true molecule overlap between CRAFT's training set and CORE239 is UNKNOWN. Any statement that the two datasets are 'largely disjoint' or 'largely overlapping' would be unfounded.

source_overlap.why: primary references are not shipped per molecule; CRAFT reports only aggregate fits, so whether the same original measurements back both studies cannot be determined.

fair_comparison.possible: model FORM decomposition on the overlapping molecules
cannot_do: run CRAFT on OUR conformer ensembles: CRAFT needs per-atom charges, atomic dipoles and per-atom polarizabilities from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB ensemble; ORCA r2SCAN-3c outputs do not carry those arrays
compare CRAFT's published CV metrics with our MAE: different molecule sets, different labels, different splits. Marked NOT_COMPARABLE.
claim CRAFT beats us or vice versa on a common benchmark: n=5 is far too small to rank two models
fair_comparison.reason_no_ranking: with n<10 overlapping molecules and different label sources, any ranking would be noise. The comparison reports physics (eps_inf route, molar volume, effective dipole) rather than accuracy.

what_craft_adds_physically: an explicit Clausius-Mossotti eps_inf from the molecular polarizability
per-atom-group scaling of polarizability (3-21 fitted scales)
polar-group-resolved dipole vectors instead of one total dipole
a group-contribution molar volume (Bouteloup & Mathieu) rather than a computed cavity volume
conformer ensembles with Boltzmann averaging of BOTH alpha and mu
what_this_project_has_that_craft_does_no: explicit r2SCAN-3c electronic structure for every molecule in the queue
a family-resolved error decomposition with measured failure mechanisms
source-independence accounting at the primary-study level
candidate-pool sensitivity of the screening metric
